title: Fifteen Winters and One Unmarked Grave
subtitle: 危险与逃生 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 危险与逃生（灾害防范·危险与逃生）
meta: 主题语境：危险与逃生（灾害防范·危险与逃生）　|　核心词汇：death　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 death 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1944 the warden ① reported a death that no family in the street would have claimed, and he said the reporting was the whole of the duty. The ② death, meaning the dying and not the record, ran fifteen winters and stayed unmarked in the yard; a death, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ death in that street had the same unmarked grave against it, and the ④ death at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last of the winter and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever mourned twice. A death, his deputy said, is nine parts silence and one part somebody willing to report; the warden said the reporting is the part that fills fifteen winters.

The clerk meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the death was the whole of the case, meaning the record and not the dying. The ⑥ death, meaning the record and not any of that, is the only thing in a case that everybody files and nobody mourns; death, he said, is either something you report or the only word that means both a dying and a record. He said the record is the part they remember.

By 1952 the ⑦ death had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the unmarked grave. The ⑧ death of the whole thing, the warden wrote in January, was one street and fifteen winters of reporting; death, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to report. She said the reporting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ death I remember is the one at the end, which was entered in 1966 and is still described as the strangest in the street. A ⑩ death, the deputy said in 1968, is the only thing that improves by being mourned; every death, she said, is a record that has agreed to look like a dying. She said the record was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 死亡；丧事（指那条街上发生的那一桩）
B. n. 死亡（指那个死亡本身，与那份记录相对）
C. 固定搭配：report a death 上报一桩死亡
D. n. 死亡（指冬日最后那一桩）
E. n. 死亡；丧亡（抽象总称，指一条街累积的丧事）
F. n. 死亡记录（指登记簿上写到、被立案的那一桩）
G. n. 死亡记录（指案卷里的那份档案）
H. n. 记录（抽象总称，指人人归档却无人哀悼的那一份）

items.q: reported a death that no family in the street would have claimed
The death, meaning the dying and not the record
the death was the whole of the case
the death had become a line in a register
The death of the whole thing
A death, the deputy said in 1968

answers.why: report a death 意为“上报一桩死亡”，1944 年管理员上报了一桩那条街上没有一家人家肯认领的死亡。
death 意为“死亡”，指那个死亡本身而不是那份记录，它在院子里历经十五个冬天而没有墓碑。
death 意为“死亡”，指那条街上每一桩死亡，每一桩都对着同一座没有标记的坟。
death 意为“死亡”，指冬日最后那一桩，是唯一有人哀悼过两次的。
death 意为“死亡记录”，指案卷里的那份档案，书记员说这份记录就是那个案卷的全部。
death 意为“记录”，指人人归档却无人哀悼的那一份而不是那个死亡本身，是案卷里人人都归档、却无人哀悼的东西。
death 意为“死亡记录”，指登记簿上写到、被立案的那一桩，到 1952 年这桩死亡成了登记簿里的一行。
death 意为“死亡、丧亡”，管理员一月写道，整件事的丧亡是一条街和十五个冬天的上报。
death 意为“死亡”，我记得的是末尾那一桩，1966 年被登记入册，至今仍被说成街上最奇的一桩。
death 为抽象总称，副手 1968 年说，一桩死亡是唯一会因为被哀悼而变得更好的东西。
